report.tagline: A UK pay-TV company that bundles live TV, Sky Sports, Netflix and other apps into one box or one smart TV, Sky Glass, paid for monthly.
report.simpleSummary: Sky is the UK's biggest pay-TV company. For a monthly fee, it gives you live channels, Sky Sports football and cricket, Sky Atlantic dramas, and apps like Netflix, all in one place with one remote. You used to need a satellite dish; now you can get it over Wi-Fi through a small box called Sky Stream or a TV with Sky built in, called Sky Glass. Sky also sells broadband and mobile, and it is owned by the US company Comcast.

overview.whatItDoes: Sky sells TV packages, sport, broadband and mobile to UK and Irish homes on monthly contracts. Its newer products, Sky Stream and Sky Glass, deliver TV over the internet and pull live channels and streaming apps into one menu. It earns from subscriptions, TV hardware, and ads on its channels.
howItWorks: Customers pick a base pack (Sky Essential TV from about £15 a month) and add Sky Sports, Cinema, Netflix or HBO Max.
Sky Glass is a TV with Sky built in; customers pay for it upfront or over 24 or 48 months.
Sky Stream is a small box that plugs into any TV and works over broadband, with no dish.
One search and one 'Playlist' cover Sky shows and apps like Netflix, Disney+ and YouTube.
Sky Sports shows Premier League, cricket, F1 and golf live.
Sky Media sells targeted TV ads (AdSmart) on Sky's channels and partners.
overview.valueProposition: For homes: one bill, one remote, one menu for live sport, channels and streaming apps, with no dish needed. For Sky: hardware and bundles that keep customers on long contracts.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: A smart TV with Sky built in, speakers, voice control and a cheaper Sky Glass Air model.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Locks in customers through hardware payments and removes the need for a dish.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: A small streaming box for any TV, working over broadband.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Cheaper way to move customers off satellite, which costs Sky more.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Live Premier League, cricket, F1, golf and more.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: The biggest reason people pay for Sky and accept higher prices.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Netflix, Disney+, HBO Max, YouTube and channels in one menu, with a shared watchlist.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Keeps Sky as the front door to TV even as people move to streaming apps.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Netflix and, from 2026, ad-supported HBO Max and Discovery+ included in Sky packs.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Adds value as Sky loses exclusive rights to new HBO shows.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Shows different TV ads to different homes based on data.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Earns more per ad than normal TV advertising.

businessModel.summary: Sky earns money from monthly TV, sport, broadband and mobile subscriptions, from selling Sky Glass TVs on finance, and from TV ads through Sky Media. Its biggest cost is sport and content rights, like the £5.2 billion Premier League deal. The goal is to keep homes on long contracts by being the one place they watch everything.

revenueStreams.detail: Essential TV and add-on packs like Sky Sports, Cinema and Netflix.
About 6.6 million broadband and 3.7 million mobile customers.
Sky Glass TVs and Sky Stream boxes, paid upfront or monthly.
Sky Media sells ads on Sky channels and partners, over £1 billion a year.
Sky's no-contract streaming service with day and month passes.

businessModel.pricing: Sky TV from about £15 a month for Essential TV. Sky Sports and other packs cost extra. Sky Glass and Sky Glass Air are paid upfront or monthly over 24 or 48 months, with prices on sky.com. Offers change often.
costDrivers: Sports rights such as the Premier League and cricket
Content deals with Netflix, HBO and others
Making Sky originals and running channels
Network costs for broadband and customer service
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take a Sky Glass home paying around £15 for Essential TV, about £30 for Sky Sports and about £13 a month for the TV over 48 months, roughly £58 a month. Much of the sport fee goes to pay rights holders. The TV payment roughly covers the cost of the TV. Sky makes its profit by keeping the home for years and adding broadband and mobile, which have lower content costs. Losing a customer early is expensive because the TV may not be fully paid.

howTheyGetUsers: Live sport, especially the Premier League
Sky Glass and Stream for homes that cannot have a dish
Deals and promotions on sky.com and comparison sites
whatBringsUsersBack: Combined menu and Playlist across apps
Long contracts and TV payment plans
growth.moat: Sky owns most UK Premier League rights until 2029 and sits between homes and many streaming services as the aggregator. Its hardware and long contracts make switching hard. But its moat is weakening as studios like HBO and Disney keep new shows for their own apps.

strengths: Most Premier League rights in the UK
Strong brand and bundle of TV, broadband and mobile
Hardware like Sky Glass that removes the dish
Big ad business with Sky Media
weaknesses: Shrinking satellite base and many job cuts
Customer service under strain after cuts
risks: Studios selling direct to consumers instead of through Sky
Cheaper or free TV services like Freely
Higher sports rights prices at the next auction
Comcast cutting investment as Sky's value falls
userComplaints: Prices rising every year and after deals end
Long contracts that are hard to leave
Buffering and lag on Sky Glass or Stream over weak Wi-Fi

improvementIdeas.idea: Seasonal Sky Sports pause that lets customers pause during summer without losing their deal.
improvementIdeas.problem: Fans cancel in summer and Sky loses them to rivals.

improvementIdeas.idea: Wi-Fi quality check and Sky booster offer before Glass or Stream setup.
improvementIdeas.problem: Buffering on weak Wi-Fi leads to complaints.

improvementIdeas.idea: Clear price-rise calculator in the app showing the bill after deals end.
improvementIdeas.problem: Customers are surprised by price jumps.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More trust and fewer angry calls.

improvementIdeas.idea: AI support assistant in the Sky app to fix common issues fast.
improvementIdeas.problem: Fewer customer service staff and long waits.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Average wait time and first-contact resolution

improvementIdeas.idea: Super-bundle that adds more streaming apps at a discount.
improvementIdeas.problem: Losing exclusive HBO shows weakens Sky's value.

pmLessons: When content moves to direct apps, an aggregator must win on convenience and price.
Hardware can lock in customers, but it adds costs if customers leave early.
Sport is a strong reason to pay but has rising costs.
Cost cuts that hurt customer service can raise churn.

interviewQuestions.question: Sky is losing exclusive HBO content. What should it do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Look at what keeps customers: sport, convenience, bundles. Propose new partners or original content and measure churn.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow Sky Glass sales?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment buyers. Look at price, finance, TV quality and bundles. Propose tests.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you reduce churn after deals end?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find why people leave. Propose clear pricing, retention offers and value reminders.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Sky sell Sky Sports only through NOW?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare revenue, churn, cannibalisation and bundle value.

interviewQuestions.question: Design an aggregator feature that keeps Sky the front door to TV.
interviewQuestions.hint: Think about search, watchlists and recommendations across apps. Measure app launches through Sky.
